title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google

facts.fact: Google states there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google.
facts.quote: There's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google.

facts.fact: Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity.
facts.quote: Local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity.

facts.fact: Google defines prominence as how well-known a business is, and says prominent places are more likely to show up in search results.
facts.quote: Prominence means how well-known a business is. Prominent places are more likely to show up in search results.

facts.fact: Google says prominence is also based on how many websites link to a business and how many reviews it has.
facts.quote: This factor’s also based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have.

facts.fact: Google says verifying a business tells Google the owner is authorized to represent it, which makes it more likely to show up in search results.
facts.quote: This tells Google that you’re authorized to represent the business, so it's more likely to show up in search results.

facts.fact: Google says businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results.
facts.quote: Businesses with complete and accurate info are more likely to show up in local search results.

facts.fact: Google says the in-store products feature is available only for retail businesses in eligible countries or regions.
facts.quote: This is available only for retail businesses in eligible countries or regions.

facts.fact: Google says that if a customer does not share their location, distance is calculated using what Google knows about that location.
facts.quote: If a customer doesn’t share where they are, Google uses what it knows about their location.
